title: Sufficient conditions for spanning $k$-trees in tough graphs
summary: The toughness of a graph $G$, denoted by $τ(G)$, is defined by $τ(G)=$min $\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}:S\subseteq V(G)$ and $c(G-S)\geq2\}$. A graph $G$ is said to be $τ$-tough if $τ(G)\geq τ$. Let $k\geq2$ be an integer. A tree $T$ is called a $k$-tree if $d_{T}(v)\leq k$ for each $v\in V(T)$, that is, the maximum degree of a $k$-tree is at most $k$. A $k$-tree $T$ is a spanning $k$-tree if $T$ is a spanning subgraph of a connected graph $G$.
